about: Stop 6 on the map page: the South Palace's Main Courtyard and the throne room's glazed facade, in UTM metres (E, N) and German-zero levels like map-plan.json. The plan is read off sheet S3.45 (Uppsala, CC BY 4.0) and printed sizes; every height and the facade's zones are guessed, and say so.

paving.src: the court's paving is not in our files: plain baked brick 33 cm square, guessed

court.src: Main Courtyard 55.6 x 60.4 m read off S3.45 (P2021 p. 103: 55 x 61 m; K1914 ch. XV: 55 x 60 m)

roof.src: a flat roof of earth over its beams behind a low parapet whose top is the walls' +23: the roof's form is not known (P2021 p. 106), so the deck, the parapet and their surfaces are guessed

room.src: S3.45: outer block 57.5 x 29.6 m, room 51.8 x 17.6 m inside, long walls 6.0 m, end walls 2.8 to 2.9 m (P2021 p. 105 to 106: 51.9 x 17.5 m)
room.hsrc: the top at about +23: walls about 10 m over the highest floor (P2021 p. 67), guessed; the roof flat, its form not known (P2021 p. 106); the ceiling at +22, guessed

doorsSrc: places on S3.45, widths 3.8, 5.8, 3.8 m (P2021 p. 103 to 104); the round arch and the crowns over the floor are guessed

leaves.src: door leaves of cedar with copper bands, the gate's kind (its inscription names leaves of cedar with copper, bronze thresholds and pivots: K1918 p. 53), applied to the throne room by us; two leaves at the main door, shown open into the room against the line of its reveals; their form, size, bands and swing are guessed after the gate's

wash.src: the mud brick under the wash in the baked brick's format, 33 cm, in courses of about 10 cm with their joints: guessed; the grain of a hand-laid gypsum wash (its unevenness, the trowel's strokes, the courses showing through where it is thin, a band of wear at the foot) is ours

niche.src: a doubly recessed niche opposite the main door, opening 8.0 m, inner step 5.85 m, first step about 1.3 m deep (S3.45; K1914 ch. XV); the second step's depth and its full height are guessed; no throne

facade.src: K1914 ch. XV: on a dark blue ground yellow columns set close together, bright blue capitals with double volutes (two rows of seven courses each, from the fitters' marks), joined by palmettes; above, a frieze of white double palmettes over a band of squares alternately yellow, black and white; white borders; every colour outlined in black
facade.guessed: the zones' heights, one tier of columns, the column pitch (four bricks), the rings' colours, the palmettes' drawing and the frieze's pitch (a brick and a half; after the Berlin panel's design, whose middle and upper parts are modern) and where the zones stop at the doors; the squares a course tall between yellow courses, so the band holds at the court's distance; a white border round each arch, the frieze's palmettes stopping whole at it

colours.src: linear albedo; white, yellow and black are the gate's (COLOURS 9 at the saturated end); the dark blue ground is ours inside the cobalt range (hue 276, chroma 20, 0.18 of the white, so it stays blue, not blue-black, in the court's shade; each brick fired lighter or darker round it), read against the original fragments of the Berlin lion panel (hue 286 to 295 as shot); the light blue is ours at the blue end of the turquoise range (hue 230, chroma 24, 0.48 of the white); no red, since where it sat is not found
